org.portico.lrc.services.sync.data

Class SyncPoint

  • java.lang.Object
    • org.portico.lrc.services.sync.data.SyncPoint
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    Serializable

    public class SyncPoint
extends Object
implements Serializable
    This class keeps track of all the information about a particular synchronization point. Each point has an associated status that spells out where in the synchronization process the point currently is. See SyncPoint.Status for more details.

    To decide who has the right to register a sync point in a distributed environment, each federate that wants to register the point must first request to do so. The federate with the lowest handle is given the right to register and announce the sync point. The point keeps track of the federate handle that has the right to register it. This value can change over time (right up until the point where the status becomes SyncPoint.Status.ANNOUNCED) as federates each request registration. After a federate has requested registration, it must wait for a period of time to see if any other federates have also done so (and it is during this time that a federate with a lower handle can grab the right to register it).

    The point also keeps track of all the federates associated with it. Generally, a sync point will be "federation-wide" (that is, meant for all federates). However, on creation, a point can have restricted membership. If this is the case, only those federates whose handles are in the sync point will be informed about its existence and only those federates will be considered when deciding is a synchronization point has been achieved or not.

      static class  SyncPoint.Status
      The current status of the sync point can be one of: REQUESTED: the local federate has requested registration of the point PENDING: some other federate has a registration request out for this point ANNOUNCED: the point has been announced ACHIEVED: the local federate has achieved the point SYNCHRONIZED: all federates have achieved the point

    • Method Detail

      • requestedRegistration

        public void requestedRegistration(int federateHandle)
        Note that the given federate has requested registration of this sync point. If the handle of the federate is lower than the handle of the current registrant, it will be changed to the new handle, otherwise no change will be made.

      • getRegistrant

        public int getRegistrant()
        This method should be called after a federate has notified the federation that it wishes to register the sync point, and it has waited an appropriate period of time for other federates requests to do the same to have been received. This method will return the handle of the federate that has the right to register the point. If multiple federates attempted to register the same sync point, the federate with the lowest handle is given the right to do so. This method will return the handle of that federate.

        If this federate doesn't know who has the right, PorticoConstants.NULL_HANDLE will be returned.

      • isFederationWide

        public boolean isFederationWide()
        Returns true if this sycn point is a federation-wide (non-restricted) point that all federates currently in a federation need to have achieved before it becomes synchronized. This method should always return the opposite of isRestricted().

      • isRestricted

        public boolean isRestricted()
        Returns true if this sync point is a restricted one (that is, it isn't federation-wide). The return value of this method should always be the opposite of isFederationWide().

      • isSynchronized

        public boolean isSynchronized(Set<Integer> allFederates)
        Tests to see if all of the federates in the given set have achieved this synchronization point yet or not.

        If this is a federation-wide synchronization point, the set of given federates should be the set of federates currently in the federation. In this case, this method will return true if all the given federate handles have been recorded as having achieved the point.

        If this is a restricted synchronization point, the set of given Tests to see if all the federates in the given set have achieved the point yet. If this is a private sync point, null should be passed for the argument (this will cause the method to use the stored set of federate handles). If this is a federation-wide sync point, a set of all the handles should be passed. Assuming that a valid set is given to the method, true will be returned if all the federates in the given set have achieved the point.

      • setStatus

        public void setStatus(SyncPoint.Status status)
        Change the status of the point. In general, this will update the status to be whatever is given as the parameter. However, to avoid potential timing problems, once a point has become SyncPoint.Status.ANNOUNCED or a status later than that, it can't go back to something like SyncPoint.Status.REQUESTED or SyncPoint.Status.PENDING. Naturally I should probably just fix any potential timing problems at the source, but it's late and I'm just being overly cautious (read: lazy).
